title: Lakes
desc: Classification and formation of lakes (from Goh Cheng Leong's Physical Geography and NCERT XI 'India: Physical Environment'): lakes formed by earth movement (tectonic, rift valley), glaciation (cirque/tarn, ribbon, kettle, rock-hollow, moraine-dammed), volcanic activity (crater, caldera, lava-blocked, subsidence), erosion (karst, wind-deflated), deposition (river/ox-bow, marine/lagoon, landslide/barrier), and human/biological activity (man-made, beaver dams); major economic and human uses of lakes; and India-specific lakes (Dal, Wular, Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri, Loktak, Vembanad) and their role in Indian river systems and physiography

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about lakes:
1. Lakes vary tremendously in size, shape, depth and mode of formation, ranging from tiny ponds to vast water bodies like the Caspian Sea.
2. Most of the world's lakes are freshwater lakes fed by rivers and with out-flowing streams, e.g. Lake Geneva and Lake Poyang.
3. Lakes are permanent, indestructible features of the earth's crust that never disappear once formed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statement 3 is incorrect — the text explicitly describes lakes as 'only temporary features of the earth's crust' that will eventually be eliminated through draining and silting, even though this may take a long time in human terms. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about basins of inland drainage:
1. In regions of low precipitation and intense evaporation, streams may drain into a lake rather than reaching the sea, forming a basin of inland drainage.
2. Because of intense evaporation, such lakes tend to be saline, as seen in the Dead Sea and the Great Salt Lake of Utah.
3. The Black Sea, despite receiving many large rivers, has a salinity of less than 17 parts per thousand — far lower than the Dead Sea's 250 parts per thousand.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's contrast between highly saline, evaporation-dominated inland drainage basins (Dead Sea, Great Salt Lake) and the much less saline Black Sea, which is diluted by numerous large inflowing rivers.

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about the elimination of lakes is NOT correct?
o: Lakes in hot deserts persist indefinitely because desert climates have no mechanism capable of removing them
Lakes are eventually eliminated through the double process of draining and silting up
In regions of unreliable rainfall, lakes may dry up completely during the dry season
In hot deserts, lakes disappear through the combined processes of evaporation, percolation and outflow
upsc.e: This statement is incorrect — the text explicitly states that in hot deserts, lakes 'disappear altogether' through evaporation, percolation and outflow, directly contradicting a claim that desert lakes persist indefinitely. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about tectonic lakes:
1. Tectonic depressions arise from the warping, sagging, bending and fracturing of the earth's crust.
2. Lake Titicaca, occupying a depression in the Andean intermont plateau at 3,810 metres above sea-level, is the highest lake in the world.
3. The Caspian Sea, the largest lake in the world, is almost five times larger than its nearest rival, Lake Superior.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's description of tectonic depression formation and its two headline examples: Lake Titicaca as the world's highest lake and the Caspian Sea as the world's largest, dwarfing Lake Superior.

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about rift valley lakes is NOT correct?
o: Rift valley lakes form where land subsides between two parallel faults, but their floors always remain well above sea-level
The East African Rift Valley extends through Zambia, Malawi, Tanzania, Kenya and Ethiopia, and along the Red Sea to Israel and Jordan
Lake Tanganyika, at 1,430 m deep, is the world's deepest lake and lies within the East African Rift Valley system
The Dead Sea, 392 metres below mean sea-level, is the world's lowest lake and is associated with rift faulting
upsc.e: This statement is incorrect — the text explicitly notes that rift valley floors are 'often below sea-level', not always well above it, as demonstrated by the Dead Sea itself lying 392 metres below sea-level. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The East African Rift Valley system contains lakes of extreme contrasting elevation, from the deep Lake Tanganyika to the low-lying Dead Sea.
Reason (R): Rift valleys form through the sinking of land between two parallel faults, producing deep, narrow, elongated troughs whose floors can lie either well above or below sea-level depending on local structural conditions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Assertion (A) and Reason (R)?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are true and R explains A — the rift valley's fault-controlled trough formation naturally produces highly variable floor elevations along its length, which is exactly why the same rift system hosts both the extremely deep Lake Tanganyika and the below-sea-level Dead Sea.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (Glacial Lake Type) with List-II (Description) and select the correct answer using the code below.
List-I:
A. Cirque lake or tarn
B. Ribbon lake
C. Kettle lake
D. Rock-hollow lake
List-II:
1. Formed by ice-scouring when valley glaciers or ice sheets scoop out hollows on the surface
2. An irregular depression in an outwash plain left by the melting of stagnant ice
3. Water filling the over-deepened floor of an armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a valley
4. A long, deep lake occupying a glacial trough
Codes:
upsc.e: The correct match is A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1: a cirque lake/tarn occupies an over-deepened cirque hollow; a ribbon lake occupies a long glacial trough; a kettle lake is an irregular depression from melted stagnant ice; and a rock-hollow lake forms through direct ice-scouring of the land surface.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about kettle lakes:
1. Kettle lakes are depressions in the outwash plain left by the melting of masses of stagnant ice.
2. They are irregular in shape because of the uneven morainic surface and are never of great size or depth.
3. Examples include the meres of Shropshire in England and the kettle-lakes of Orkney in Scotland.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's description of kettle lake formation from stagnant ice melt, their characteristic irregularity and small scale, and its two named examples in England and Scotland.

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about lakes formed by moraine damming and glacial drift deposition is NOT correct?
o: Finland's abundant glacial lakes are entirely unrelated to moraine damming and instead all originate from wind deflation
Both lateral and terminal moraines are capable of damming valleys to form lakes, e.g. Lake Windermere in England's Lake District
In glaciated lowlands with a drumlin landscape, poor drainage between drumlins can create small water-logged lakes, e.g. those of County Down in Northern Ireland
Finland is nicknamed 'the Land of Lakes' (Suomi) and is said to contain over 35,000 glacial lakes scoured out by ice action
upsc.e: This statement is incorrect — Finland's glacial lakes are explicitly attributed to ice-scouring (rock-hollow lake formation), not wind deflation, which is an entirely different (desert-related) process described elsewhere in the chapter. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about volcanic lakes:
1. A crater lake forms when rain falls into a dormant or extinct volcano's crater, which has no superficial outlet.
2. A caldera is an enlargement of a crater through subsidence, and Crater Lake in Oregon, U.S.A. actually occupies a caldera rather than a simple crater.
3. Lake Toba in northern Sumatra and Lake Avernus near Naples are both cited as examples of crater/caldera lakes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's description of crater versus caldera lake formation and its three named examples: Crater Lake (Oregon, in a caldera), Lake Toba (Sumatra), and Lake Avernus (near Naples).

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about lava-blocked and subsidence lakes is NOT correct?
o: The Sea of Galilee formed when a lava flow blocked the Jordan valley, and it functions as an outward-draining lake with a major river outlet
Myvatn in Iceland formed through the subsidence of the crust of a hollow lava flow, leaving a wide, shallow depression
A lava-blocked lake forms when a solidified lava stream dams a river across a valley
Lakes formed by volcanic subsidence result from the collapse of the crust of a hollow lava flow rather than from crater filling
upsc.e: This statement is incorrect — the Sea of Galilee is explicitly described in the text as 'an inland lake', meaning it lacks an outward drainage outlet to the sea, not a lake with a major outward-draining river outlet. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about karst lakes:
1. Karst lakes may form when solution hollows in limestone, carved by rain-water, become clogged with debris.
2. The collapse of limestone roofs of underground caverns may expose long, narrow lakes that were once entirely underground, e.g. Lac de Chaillexon in the Jura Mountains.
3. Poljes, which normally lack surface outlets, may contain lakes that expand during wet periods and shrink during dry periods due to seepage, e.g. Lake Scutari in Yugoslavia.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's account of karst lake formation via solution-hollow clogging, cavern-roof collapse exposing former underground lakes, and polje lakes that fluctuate seasonally due to seepage.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about wind-deflated lakes:
1. The deflating action of winds in deserts creates hollows that may reach the groundwater table, forming small, shallow lakes.
2. Excessive evaporation of wind-deflated lakes often turns them into salt lakes and playas.
3. Wind-deflated lakes are found in the Qattara Depression in Egypt and the Great Basin of Utah, U.S.A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's description of wind-deflation hollow formation, their conversion into salt lakes/playas through evaporation, and the two named desert examples.

upsc.q: Which one of the following is NOT a correct example of local subsidence caused by the solutional removal of underlying rock salt, as described in the text?
o: Lake Titicaca in the Andean plateau of South America
Many of the meres of Cheshire, England
Meres partly resulting from salt-mining operations in Cheshire
Local subsidence when underlying beds of rock salt are gradually removed in solution
upsc.e: Lake Titicaca is a tectonic lake formed by crustal warping in the Andes, entirely unrelated to rock-salt solution subsidence; it does not belong among the Cheshire-type salt-solution meres described in the text, unlike the other three options.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about depositional lakes:
1. An ox-bow lake forms when a river shortens its course during a flood by cutting across a meandering loop, leaving a horseshoe-shaped channel.
2. Lagoons formed by spits or bars built by wind and wave action along coasts are called 'haffs' in East Germany and Poland.
3. Barrier lakes, formed by landslides, screes or avalanches blocking valleys, tend to be long-lived and geologically stable because their debris dams never fail.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statement 3 is incorrect — the text explicitly describes barrier lakes as 'short-lived, because the loose fragments that pile across the valleys will soon give way under the pressure of water', causing sudden floods when they fail, not remaining geologically stable. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about marine-deposit lagoons is NOT correct?
o: Lagoons enclosed by spits or bars are always deep, permanent water bodies unaffected by tidal cycles
Lagoons of this type are commonly found off the deltas of large rivers such as the Nile and the Ganges
Strong on-shore winds can push coastal sand dunes landwards, enclosing marshy lagoons, as seen in the Landes of south-west France
Because such lagoons are enclosed only by a narrow spit of land, they may drain away at low tide
upsc.e: This statement is incorrect — the text explicitly notes such lagoons 'may drain away at low tide' because they are shallow and enclosed only by a narrow spit, contradicting a claim that they are deep and unaffected by tides. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about human and biological lake formation:
1. Lake Mead, formed above the Hoover Dam on the Colorado River, U.S.A., is cited as the most imposing man-made lake.
2. Beavers construct dams across rivers with timber, forming quite permanent lakes such as Beaver Lake in Yellowstone National Park.
3. Ornamental lakes made to attract tourists, and lakes created by mining activities such as tin mining in Peninsular Malaysia, are also examples of human-influenced lakes.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's examples of dam-created lakes (Lake Mead), animal-made lakes (beaver dams), and other human-influenced lakes (ornamental lakes, mining-created lakes).

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence waterway system:
1. It penetrates more than 2,740 km into the interior of North America and is used as a chief artery of commerce.
2. The annual tonnage passing through the Sault-Ste. Marie (Soo) Canal is estimated to be greater than the combined annual tonnage of the Suez and Panama Canals.
3. The 'HOMES' lakes (Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, Superior) were central to the development of one of the world's greatest industrial districts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's description of the Great Lakes waterway's length and commercial role, the exceptional traffic through the Soo Canal, and the industrial significance of the HOMES lakes region.

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about lakes and hydro-electric power generation is NOT correct?
o: Artificial reservoirs are always preferred over natural lakes for hydro-electric power because their water flow is more variable and therefore more efficient to harness
Natural lakes are preferred to artificial reservoirs because the volume of water flowing from them varies very little throughout the year
The Niagara River, flowing from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario, has a very regular water supply for its power stations
The Catawba River in the Carolinas, which does not flow from a lake, has very little water during the dry season, at times forcing cotton mills to close
upsc.e: This statement is incorrect and reverses the text's actual claim — natural lakes are preferred BECAUSE their outflow varies very little through the year (steadier supply), not because artificial reservoirs have more variable, supposedly more efficient flow. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about lakes regulating river flow and moderating climate:
1. A river with large lakes in its basin seldom experiences serious floods, since the lake absorbs excess water during heavy rain and releases it steadily in the dry season.
2. Rivers leaving lakes tend to have clearer water because lakes retain part of the sediment load.
3. Large, deep lakes have no measurable effect on the temperature or precipitation of the surrounding region, behaving exactly like dry land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statement 3 is incorrect — the text explicitly states large, deep lakes moderate regional climate much like oceans do, citing milder winters on the eastern shores of Lakes Erie, Ontario and Huron and a slight influence on cloudiness/precipitation near Lake Michigan. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the economic uses of lakes:
1. When lakes dry up, their former beds may become highly fertile agricultural land, as in the Vale of Pickering, Yorkshire, or the Red River Valley of Canada (former site of Lake Agassiz).
2. Salt lakes such as the Dead Sea are evaporated to produce common salt, and borax is mined in the salt lakes of the Mojave Desert.
3. Gypsum mined near Cheshire and Stassfurt (near Berlin) is unrelated to any lake or evaporite deposit and originates purely from volcanic rock.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — the text explicitly states these gypsum, potash and chemical deposits at Cheshire and Stassfurt were 'obtained from deposits formed in an earlier geological period' associated with evaporite/salt lake processes, not from volcanic rock.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about Dal Lake and the Jhelum river in the Kashmir Valley, as described in NCERT's account of Indian physiography:
1. The Jhelum in the Kashmir Valley is still in its youth stage of development, yet it forms meanders, a feature typically associated with a river's mature stage.
2. This unusual meandering is explained by the local base level provided by an erstwhile, much larger lake, of which the present Dal Lake is only a small remaining part.
3. Dal Lake is located near Srinagar, the capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct. NCERT specifically uses Dal Lake and the Jhelum's meanders as an example of how a lake can influence a river's evolutionary behaviour independent of its overall developmental stage, by providing a local base level.

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about lakes of the Ladakh/Kashmir Himalayan region is NOT correct?
o: Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri are freshwater lakes, while Dal and Wular are salt-water lakes
The Wular lake lies along the course of the Jhelum river before it enters Pakistan through a deep gorge
Dal and Wular are examples of fresh lakes found in this Himalayan region
Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri are examples of salt-water lakes found in this Himalayan region
upsc.e: This statement reverses the correct classification — NCERT specifically identifies Dal and Wular as fresh lakes and Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri as salt-water lakes, not the other way around. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q: According to NCERT, in which Indian state is Loktak lake, a large lake surrounded by mountains on all sides forming a distinctive physiographic feature, situated?
upsc.e: Loktak lake is situated in Manipur, where it forms a unique physiographic feature at the centre of the state, surrounded by mountains from all sides — directly from NCERT's own sample objective question on this topic.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about lakes and lagoons mentioned in NCERT's account of Indian rivers:
1. The Brahmaputra originates in the Chemayungdung glacier of the Kailash range near the Mansarovar lake in Tibet.
2. The Pamba river of Kerala, after a course of 177 km, falls into the Vembanad lake, part of a backwater system used for fishing, navigation and tourism, including the Nehru Trophy boat race.
3. Streams that terminate by joining an inland lake or playa typically carry pure, mineral-free water unsuitable for any commercial salt extraction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statement 3 is incorrect — NCERT explicitly notes that such terminal lakes and playas have brackish water, which is 'the main source of obtaining salt' in those regions, the opposite of being unsuitable for salt extraction. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

upsc.q:
How many of the following lakes mentioned in the NCERT account of Indian physiography and drainage are correctly classified as freshwater (not salt-water) lakes?
1. Dal Lake
2. Wular Lake
3. Pangong Tso
4. Tso Moriri
upsc.e: Only Dal Lake and Wular Lake are classified as freshwater lakes in the text; Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri are explicitly described as salt-water lakes of the same Himalayan region, so only two of the four listed lakes are freshwater.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about lakes as a source of food:
1. Sturgeon is commercially caught in the Caspian Sea.
2. Salmon and sea trout are caught in the Great Lakes, and fishing is a leading occupation on Tonle Sap in Kampuchea.
3. Countries such as China, Japan and Singapore have developed artificial lakes specifically for inland fish breeding.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's specific examples of commercial and subsistence fishing in the Caspian Sea, the Great Lakes, and Tonle Sap, plus the deliberate creation of artificial fish-breeding lakes in East and Southeast Asia.

upsc.q: Which one of the following statements about lakes used for irrigation and multi-purpose dam projects is NOT correct?
o: The Sennar Dam on the Blue Nile (Sudan) and the Ghulam Mohammed Barrage on the Indus (Pakistan) are examples of dams built purely for hydro-electric power with no irrigation function
Modern multi-purpose dams typically combine hydro-electric power generation with irrigation water supply
The Burrinjuck Dam is located on the Murrumbidgee river in Australia
Former lake beds, once dried up, may be covered with fertile alluvium suitable for agriculture, as with the Red River Valley of Canada (former site of Lake Agassiz)
upsc.e: This statement is incorrect — the text explicitly lists the Sennar Dam and Ghulam Mohammed Barrage as examples of dams that ALSO supply water for irrigation alongside their other functions, not as purely power-generation projects with no irrigation role. The other three statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about lakes that help regulate river flow:
1. The Poyang and Dongting lakes on the Chang Jiang (Yangtze), Tonle Sap on a Mekong tributary, and Lake Constance on the upper Rhine are all cited as flow-regulating lakes.
2. Where such natural flow-regulating lakes are unavailable and flooding is a serious problem, artificial reservoirs like the Hoover Dam or the Bhakra and Nangal Dams on the Sutlej in India may be built instead.
3. Flow-regulating lakes work by absorbing excess water during heavy rain and releasing it gradually, but they have no effect on a river's sediment load.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — the text explicitly notes that 'because lakes retain part of the sediment load, rivers leaving lakes have clearer water', showing that lakes DO measurably affect sediment load, contrary to the claim.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about lakes as tourist attractions:
1. Lake Geneva, Lake Lucerne, Lake Lugano and Lake Como are all cited as well-known lakeside holiday and health resort destinations.
2. The glacier-formed lakes of the Alps have made tourism a national occupation of the Swiss.
3. Lake Placid in New York, and Lake Vaner and Lake Vatter in Sweden, are also mentioned as notable lakeside tourist destinations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct, matching the text's list of major lakeside tourism destinations across Switzerland, the United States, and Sweden, and its specific note about tourism's national importance around the Alpine glacial lakes.
